subject: math
title: A-Math quadratics: completing the square, discriminant and inequalities

scenes.caption: Completing the square, as area
scenes.narration: Take x squared plus six x, built as area: an x-by-x square with two three-by-x strips. Slide one strip below the square, then the missing three-by-three corner slides in to complete it.

shape.explain: The starting point: x squared plus six x, drawn as area.
The x-by-x square: the geometric picture of x squared.
A three-by-x strip: half of the 6x, slid below the square.
The second three-by-x strip: 6x split into two equal parts.
The missing corner: a three-by-three square of area 9.
The completed square: x plus 3, all squared, minus 9.

steps.text: Half of 6 is 3; the missing square is 3² = 9

scenes.caption: The discriminant decides the roots
scenes.narration: For a-x-squared plus b-x plus c, the discriminant D equals b squared minus four a c. Watch one parabola sink: above the axis is D negative, touching is D zero, crossing twice is D positive.

shape.explain: The discriminant: D equals b squared minus four a c.
shape.tex: f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c, \quad D = b^2 - 4ac

shape.explain: The x-axis: roots are where the curve crosses or touches it.
The parabola: its position against the x-axis tells the sign of D.
D negative: the curve misses the axis, no real roots.
D zero: the curve just touches the axis, one repeated root.
The touching point: the single repeated root where the curve meets the axis.
D positive: the curve crosses twice, two real roots.
The left root: one of the two crossings.
The right root: one of the two crossings.

steps.text: The sign of D is the whole story

scenes.caption: Quadratic inequalities on a number line
scenes.narration: For x squared minus four greater than zero, first find the roots: negative two and two. A test probe travels the number line — regions where the test passes light up green.

shape.explain: The inequality: x squared minus four is greater than zero.
The number line: test each region the roots cut out.
A root: x equals negative 2, where the expression is zero.
A root: x equals 2, where the expression is zero.
D negative: the curve misses the axis, no real roots.
D positive: the curve crosses twice, two real roots.
A test value: check whether the inequality holds here.
A passing region: every x here satisfies the inequality.
A test value: check whether the inequality holds here.
A passing region: every x here satisfies the inequality.
The solution: x less than negative 2 or x greater than 2.

steps.text: Roots first, then test each region

scenes.caption: A common mistake: a negative discriminant means no solution
scenes.narration: A negative discriminant means the equation has no solution. No real roots is read as no solutions at all. But no real roots is not no solution: the equation still has two complex roots. The curve never touches the real axis and the roots dive off the real line: two complex solutions.

shape.explain: The example: a quadratic whose discriminant is negative.
The x-axis: roots are where the curve crosses or touches it.
The parabola: its position against the x-axis tells the sign of D.
The claim: no real roots. Read the word real.
The imaginary direction: where the two complex roots sit.
A complex root: it sits off the real line.
A complex root: it sits off the real line.
The truth: no real roots is not no solution.

steps.text: No real roots — read the word real
